done_when: forge story new <KEY> "<title>" works for a story that has no spec: the story's own branch adds it to the roadmap, the plan's Why carries the problem, and the story gets one read loop and one approval; stories made from a spec work as today and specs stay optional. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Functional. When `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix <fix>` promotes a fix, this line adds a missing roadmap entry only to `story/<KEY>`. `_promote` in `src/forge/story.py:928` renames the existing fix branch to `task/<KEY>-SPEC` without copying that entry. The new carry logic in `src/forge/task.py:139` runs only for `forge task start`, so it does not cover promotion. A promoted story with just its SPEC task can therefore merge without its roadmap entry. The changed guide explicitly includes stories promoted from fixes; `test_22_promote` checks the story branch's roadmap but not the promoted task branch.
findings.title: Promoted stories leave their roadmap entry off the task branch

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow: a fix promoted to a story keeps today's roadmap route; only brand-new stories start from a one-line goal

why: A new story needs a spec, its own read loop, a confirmation and a roadmap fix before its plan can even start
